content:
maya: FYI seeing a regression after flipping the prefetch gate timer to 12ms in canary. Stream lat p50 up ~8ms, p95 up ~45ms.
maya: repro steps: enable gate=12ms, token_budget_target=16, kv_prefetch=on for chat-long workload.
maya: snippet from traces (short):
```
stream_send() +0.6ms
partial_decode: wait 9.4ms
kv_lookup: 1.2ms (cold)
flush_timer fired @12.1ms -> forced send
```
sam: interesting — sounds like flush timer is preempting partial-decode completion and causing early sends that miss kv warmup.
sam: can you paste the admission queue stats around the event? how many coalesced reqs?
maya: queue snapshot: `len=3, avg_tokens=18, target=16, pending_bytes=~4k`
maya: trace shows the kernel selected was small-kernel path, but partial-decode still ongoing so we got a tiny batch and then flush.
lee: so we lose batching efficiency and also KV didn’t warmup -> extra oracle fetch on GPU -> stalls.
lee: hypothesis: gate timer too aggressive relative to partial-decode slack + token_budget variance. should bias timer based on per-request decode-start percentile.
anita: can we try adaptive_gate = max( min_timer, p90_partial_decode + margin ) and baseline margin 2ms?
anita: proposed config: `gate_base_ms=6, gate_margin_ms=2, gate_max=30, use_request_p90=true`
maya: ran offline sim with logs from yesterday — using p90-adaptive reduced p95 by ~22ms in simulation and improved AVG tokens/batch from 7->13.
maya: but one caveat: when request size skew high, p90 estimate is noisy. we need smoothing window 30s.
sam: also check kernel selection churn — earlier we saw switch to big-kernel causing higher tail. maybe timer influenced kernel pick due to different batch size.
sam: add probe that tags each batch with `kernel_hint` and `gate_reason` in traces.
infra-bot: deploy patch candidate:r/stream-gate-adaptive-2026-03-18 to canary (3 hosts) scheduled.
lee: quick perf profile from canary (cpu/gpu): `gpu_util 67%, kernel_launch_time +3ms per batch`
lee: kernel launch penalty only becomes dominant on tiny batches; so the adaptive gate both increases batch size and reduces kernel-launch overhead.
maya: one more wrinkle: KV cache miss penalty is variable by model length (more prompts -> bigger keyspace -> slower lookup) — adding lookup latency histogram to the sample should help.
anita: action items: (1) flip in canary the adaptive_gate with 30s smoothing, (2) instrument batch tags (kernel_hint, kv_miss), (3) run 8h perf run on chat-long and chat-short.
maya: assigning (1) @infra-bot -> infra deploy, (2) @lee -> tag instrumentation, (3) @sam -> config validation and telemetry.
sam: noted — will validate telemetry schema then roll.
lee: I’ll add kv_miss histogram and batch tags. expect a PR by EOD.
maya: if canary looks good, roll to dedicated pool tomorrow morning low-traffic window. :thumbsup:
sam: also we should add a safety fall-back: if p95 latency increases >30ms post-roll for 10m, automatic revert.
anita: agreed, add to rollout playbook.
maya: thanks all — will post canary results in ~4h.
